spine: 1. Meta 廣告服務把艦隊升到 Linux 6.9 後，取代 CFS 的新排程器 EEVDF 造成延遲退步，一部分主機被迫留在舊的 6.4，艦隊被迫分裂並背上維運技術債。
2. 通用排程器 CFS/EEVDF 的共同問題是「balance threads across CPUs with no understanding of the workload」——分不出誰是使用者在等的請求、誰是可以晚跑的背景工作。
3. sched_ext 是一個 BPF-based、正式進 Linux 主線是 v6.12 的可擴充排程框架，讓排程 policy 寫成使用者空間的 BPF 程式而非焊死在 kernel 裡。
4. Meta 自製的 policy 靠「domain-specific knowledge」把 CPU 軟性切成兩個 pool：延遲敏感的 request path 與較不敏感的背景工作，並靠 wake-up/enqueue/dispatch/idle 四個 callback 決定分配。
5. 首發把最大量的伺服器一次從 6.4+CFS 升到 6.9+sched_ext：p99 降 28%、全機隊省電 3.28 MW、weighted-ads-ranked +1.1%。
6. 因為 policy 活在使用者空間，後續兩次迭代不必等 kernel release，「shipped in days rather than months」，再把 p99 砍 60%、timeout error 降 18%。
7. 這個交付節奏把 sched_ext 從「kernel 升級的絆腳石」變成「持續優化平台」——比任何單一數字更重要的是排程優化從一次性專案變成日常可迭代的動作。

perspective.mechanism: sched_ext 讓一份 BPF 程式在使用者空間定義排程 policy，透過 wake-up / enqueue / dispatch / idle 四個 event-driven callback 跟 kernel 交握，比在 kernel 裡改一個通用排程演算法快得多；Meta 的 policy 靠 domain-specific knowledge 把 CPU 軟性切成兩個 pool（延遲敏感 request path、較不敏感的背景工作）。
perspective.tradeoff: 換來的是 workload-specific 的延遲、耗電、排序品質同時改善，代價是每個服務都得自己寫一份 policy——sched_ext 給的是框架而非現成排程器；文章顯示 Meta 首發用的是 6.9 kernel，早於 sched_ext 官方進主線的 6.12，意味著在正式合流前就要自行維護 backport 才能用上這套框架。
perspective.reader_use: 在 Linux ≥6.12（或已自行 backport sched_ext 的內部 kernel）上跑延遲敏感混合工作負載（前景請求 + 背景任務）的工程師，可以考慮用 sched_ext 取代等待上游 CFS/EEVDF 調整，把「前景優先、背景讓路」寫成一份可以獨立於 kernel release 節奏迭代的 BPF policy。

notes.quote: When upgrading to Linux kernel 6.9, Meta's ads infrastructure encountered latency regressions from the newly introduced Earliest Eligible Virtual Deadline First (EEVDF) scheduler, which replaced the older CFS scheduler.
notes.interpretation: The kernel 6.4 to 6.9 upgrade path was the direct trigger of the latency regression; EEVDF replacing CFS is presented as a plain fact, not a hedged possibility.

notes.quote: This regression reduced ad ranking capacity, forcing a subset of ad hosts to remain on the older kernel 6.4, creating technical debt and operational fragmentation.
notes.interpretation: The regression had a direct business-capacity cost (not just a synthetic benchmark number), and the mitigation (keeping some hosts on 6.4) itself created a second-order operational cost.

notes.quote: balance threads across CPUs with no understanding of the workload
notes.interpretation: Describes the structural limitation shared by general-purpose schedulers (CFS and EEVDF alike): fairness is computed without any notion of which thread is latency-critical.

notes.quote: an open-source, BPF-based scheduler framework that officially entered kernel v6.12
notes.interpretation: sched_ext's official upstream merge point is v6.12 — later than the 6.9 kernel Meta's initial sched_ext launch ran on, implying Meta used an internal backport ahead of upstream merge (marked as inference in the post, not asserted as sourced fact).

notes.quote: The policy soft-partitions CPUs into two pools, one for threads on the latency-critical request path and one for less latency-sensitive work.
notes.interpretation: The core mechanism of Meta's custom scheduler: a soft (dynamically adjustable) two-pool partition, not a hard pinned split.

notes.quote: the domain-specific knowledge encoded inside the policy
notes.interpretation: The pool-assignment decision is possible only because the policy is written with knowledge of what each thread in the ads-serving workload actually does — the exact capability CFS/EEVDF lack.

notes.quote: Work that improves the p99 request latency is scheduled first, and everything else takes a back seat.
notes.interpretation: States the policy's priority ordering plainly — latency-critical work always wins, framed as an unconditional rule rather than a soft preference.

notes.quote: the scheduler policy lives in user space as a BPF program
notes.interpretation: Explains why iteration is fast: the policy is not compiled into the kernel image, so changes don't require a kernel rebuild/reboot/release cycle.

notes.quote: The system operates through event-driven callbacks including thread wake-up, enqueue, dispatch, and idle transitions.
notes.interpretation: Names the four hook points where the BPF policy makes scheduling decisions — used as the basis for the hero widget's 'BPF policy path' annotation.

notes.quote: 28% reduction in service p99 latency on ads retrieval
notes.interpretation: Headline result of the initial sched_ext launch, specific to the ads retrieval stage (not a fleet-wide average across all stages).

notes.quote: 3.28 megawatts power savings
notes.interpretation: Fleet-wide power savings figure attributed to the initial launch, presented alongside the latency and ranking numbers as a joint result.

notes.quote: 1.1% increase in weighted-ads-ranked
notes.interpretation: A business-quality metric improving alongside latency and power — used in the post to argue the three outcomes moved together, not traded off against each other.

notes.quote: Additional 60% p99 latency reduction
notes.interpretation: Follow-on user-space-only policy iterations produced a further, larger latency reduction on top of the initial launch's 28%.

notes.quote: 18% reduction in timeout errors
notes.interpretation: A reliability metric (timeout errors on the critical path) improved alongside the latency gain in the follow-on iterations.

notes.quote: Each follow-on iteration above shipped in days rather than months because the scheduler policy lives in user space as a BPF program.
notes.interpretation: Directly ties the fast iteration cadence to the user-space BPF architecture — the causal claim used as the spine of the post's fourth section.

notes.quote: That cadence is what turned sched_ext from a 'kernel upgrade unblocker' to a continuous-optimization platform for ads serving.
notes.interpretation: The article's own framing of the strategic shift — used verbatim as the post's closing argument rather than paraphrased into a stronger claim.

notes.quote: POSTED ON JULY 13, 2026 / By Blaise Sanouillet, Sunyi Shao, Jeff Song, Gosh Arzumanyan, Shawn Wu, Tejun Heo, Praveen Sampath, GP Musumeci
notes.interpretation: Publication date and author byline, used to confirm the source's recency and authorship; not directly quoted in the post prose.

notes.quote: This approach tends to keep related work on the same CPUs over time, improving last-level cache (L3) locality and reducing costly DRAM access.
notes.interpretation: Gives the causal mechanism linking the two-pool design to BOTH the latency win and the power-savings win: keeping related work co-located reduces L3 cache misses and DRAM round-trips, which cuts both wait time and energy.

notes.quote: The size of each pool is adjusted dynamically using load-based heuristics.
notes.interpretation: Confirms the 'soft' in soft-partition: pool boundaries move with load rather than being fixed at deploy time.

notes.quote: Measured by backtest after the rollout reached global scale and stabilized (~3 weeks)
notes.interpretation: Gives the measurement window for the initial-launch headline numbers: they were backtested about three weeks after global rollout stabilized, not measured day-one.

notes.quote: Two follow-on scheduler-policy updates, delivered as purely user-space changes, extended the win
notes.interpretation: Confirms there were exactly two follow-on policy updates, and that the article reports their combined effect (60% additional p99, 18% timeout reduction) rather than breaking out each update's individual contribution.

notes.quote: 1.6% CPU-utilization reduction
notes.interpretation: A footnoted supporting metric alongside the 3.28 MW power-savings figure — fleet-wide CPU utilization dropped 1.6 percentage points, directionally consistent with the cache-locality mechanism (n18) reducing wasted cycles spent stalled on DRAM access.
